Silica Analyzer Working Principle From Sample to ppb Reading

The silica analyzer working principle is colorimetry: dissolved reactive silica is turned into a coloured complex, and the amount of light that the solution absorbs is converted into a concentration. Absorbance follows the Beer Lambert law, A = ε × l × c, where ε is the absorptivity, l is the cell path length and c is the concentration. With ε and l fixed by the instrument, absorbance is directly proportional to silica.

StageWhat happensWhy it matters
Blank readingPhotometer reads the sample before colour developsCancels natural colour and turbidity
Molybdate reactionSilica forms yellow silicomolybdic acidStarts the selective reaction
Phosphate removalCitric or oxalic acid destroys the phosphate complexStops phosphate reading as silica
ReductionYellow complex becomes intense molybdenum blueMuch higher sensitivity for ppb levels
Colour readingAbsorbance measured at the blue wavelengthDifference from blank gives net absorbance
CalculationCalibration curve converts absorbance to ppbResult sent to DCS and alarms

Because the measurement is a difference between two readings in the same cell, drift from window fouling largely cancels. Stable cell temperature keeps the reaction time and colour intensity repeatable, which is essential when steam limits are only a few ppb.
